In Ovid's version, Daedalus warned Icarus not to fly too high or too low. The sea where he fell is still called the Icarian Sea.

#greekmythology #icarus #shorts

lines.text: Everyone remembers: don't fly too close to the sun. But that was only half the warning.
The inventor Daedalus and his son Icarus were trapped on Crete by King Minos.
So Daedalus built wings, from feathers, thread and wax.
His warning: don't fly too high, or the sun will melt the wax. And don't fly too low, or the sea spray will soak the feathers.
Icarus flew higher and higher. The wax melted, and he fell into the sea.
That sea is still called the Icarian Sea, beside the Greek island of Icaria.
The real lesson? Fly the middle path.
